title: Redline Snap row stops cutting Edges and centers
goal: In the redline properties panel, the Snap setting reads "Edges and centers" but the last letter is sliced off. This makes the setting readable at the panel's normal width.
notes: redline.html Tool options section. Measured 2026-08-23 at the 267px dock: the .lead gets 102px for 104px of content, so it clips by 2px with no ellipsis (flex + overflow:hidden hard-cuts). Two-item row, no trailing action, so .irow.stacked and .irow.wide are both heavier than the problem. Proven dead end: you cannot make the 76px label track yield to the value in CSS grid. minmax(0,76px) on the label plus min-width:max-content on the value overflows the row in Chrome (label stays 76, select grows to 126, row total 255.6 vs 232); min(max-content,100%) resolves to 100% and changes nothing; fit-content(76px) works but shrinks the label to 27px and breaks the label column alignment with the neighbouring rows. So the fix is either a shorter value string or a per-section label width.
acceptance: At the default panel width the Snap value reads in full, with nothing cut off
The Snap row still lines up with the Units and Show rows above and below it
The row is measured in a browser at the default panel width before and after, and the numbers are recorded in the task log
